dialectRules.rule: Address users consistently with formal Sie/Ihr forms; never use du/dein forms in user-facing copy.
dialectRules.notes: Formal forms heavily dominate the de files (for example, common.json uses „Aktualisieren Sie …“). Legacy du strings remain mainly in client-portal.json, features/tickets.json, and common.json and are inconsistencies, not precedent.

dialectRules.rule: Capitalize every German noun, including nouns inside labels and compounds.
dialectRules.notes: Examples: Rechnung, Zeiteintrag, Kundenportal, E-Mail-Adresse. Preserve brand casing and all-uppercase abbreviations.

dialectRules.rule: Prefer idiomatic German compounds and use linking hyphens around abbreviations or English loanword components where readability requires them.
dialectRules.notes: Examples: Kundenportal, Servicekatalog, Stundenkontingent, E-Mail-Adresse, SLA-Vereinbarung, Onboarding-Assistent. Avoid English-style spaced noun stacks.

dialectRules.rule: Keep Ticket for support work and translate a sales quote as Angebot.
dialectRules.notes: Ticket is neuter (das Ticket); Angebot is neuter (das Angebot). Travel/admission terms and Zitat are forbidden.

dialectRules.rule: Keep Abrechnung (billing), Rechnung (invoice), Rechnungsstellung (invoicing), and Gutschrift (credit) distinct.
dialectRules.notes: These entities coexist in the billing UI and must not collapse into Rechnung or Kredit indiscriminately.

dialectRules.rule: Retain established German MSP/software loanwords and give them normal German articles and plural forms.
dialectRules.notes: Examples: das Asset/die Assets, das Board/die Boards, das Dashboard, der Job/die Jobs, das Ticket/die Tickets, der Workflow/die Workflows, der Webhook/die Webhooks.

dialectRules.rule: Preserve every {{variable}} exactly as in the English source.
dialectRules.notes: Do not translate placeholders, braces, or variable names.

exact: phase_name, task_description, assigned_to, estimated_hours, due_date, priority, service, task_type, status, tags
identicalAllowlist.notes: This allowlist is intentionally conservative; audit tooling should report English-identical German strings unless they match one of these exact values, case-insensitive established loanwords, or technical patterns.
